items.name: Blue Mountains Dawn
items.subtitle: Spinebills, king parrots and a lyrebird in the first light · Faulconbridge, New South Wales

xc.species: Dawn chorus, with a superb lyrebird
xc.location: Faulconbridge, Blue Mountains, New South Wales
xc.remarks: This is a longer version of XC441640 but is still trimmed, but also normalized. Modified from the above: Trimmed a few snippets which don't interfere with vocalizations. In order of first vocalization (+ indicates occurs more times): Menura novaehollandiae (from very start, ongoing), 11:40 superb lyrebird from 0:07 Alisterus scapularis / australian king parrot p. 0:17 , Cracticus torquatus 0:24 +, 14:30 , 17:45 Eastern spinebill, Acanthorhynchus tenuirostris 0:28 + 2:30 , 3:00 , 4:10 , 7:28 , 10:17 Phylidonyris novaehollandiae 0:42 + 3:18 , 6:41 , 9:55 satin bowerbird / Ptilonorhynchus violaceus 2:08 , 10:20 Australian raven / Corvus coronoides 2:30 , 8:25 Wonga pigeon, Leucosarcia melanoleuca 2:35 onwards trichoglossus moluccanus ~ 3:00 + 3:50 , australian king parrot 5:10 , 8:55 , calls, flight calls, 14:40 + (flies closer and by at 15:00 , again at 16:05 ) Anthochaera carunculata / red w. 5:40 yellow-faced honeyeater / Caligavis chrysops 5:52 , 10:05 eastern yellow robin / Eopsaltria australis 5:58 (ee-chong-wee), 11:30 pied currawong / Strepera graculina 10:15 , 10:35 + satin bowerbird 10:20 also 10:26 ? The latter may be a yellow-faced honeyeater (choughs) brown thornbill 10:28 (which-is-it) sulphur-crested cockatoo / Cacatua galerita 12:30 +, 16:46 ? soft piping calls of eastern spinebill or eastern yellow robin grey shrikethrush 15:23 , 16:30 , 16:55 These birds have been seen nearby on other occasions, with the exceptions of the EYR Changed the encoding to 144 kbps to fit in the 20 MB file size, I don't think it has made a noticeable difference to the quality of sound. If others want to listen to the rest and send me additions, feel free to do so. Recorded on a deck at the back of the house at the provided coordinates, about 5-10 m above ground. This is typical dry sclerophyll forest on a ridge with eucalypts and casuarinas dominating the canopy, in different areas. There are intermittent creeks (more like ponds along the creekline as of Nov 2018) at the valley bottoms east and west about 200 m away. I have deliberately not trimmed some noises in some of my uploads as even though they don't overlap with vocalizations, trimming them reduces the time between vocalizations, which results in lost important information. Feel free to send me additions for background species or suggestions for my recordings, or upload your edited version of the recording, linking to the original and letting me know. My recording device is a smart phone, a Xiaomi Redmi Note 4X. Recorded straight to mp3.
